definitions.name: talk_list_conversations
definitions.description: Lists the Talk conversations the authenticated user takes part in, with the number of unread messages Talk shows in its own list. When that count cannot be read, the conversation is still listed and unreadMessages is null. A conversation the lobby bars is still listed and unreadMessages is 0. A lobby whose timer has already passed is treated as open for this answer only, and a lobby that cannot be read counts as closed. The display name is the name Talk already stored: a direct conversation names the other participant from the stored pair of account ids, or from the participants already in the room when the stored name is empty or still the legacy account id, and the name is empty when that read fails or the other participant cannot be identified, a group with no stored name is empty, and the release notes conversation and a password request use the names Talk gives them. It changes no state: it does not mark anything as read, does not open a lobby, does not rename a conversation, does not touch notifications and does not touch activity.

definitions.name: talk_read_messages
definitions.description: Reads the latest messages of a conversation, without marking anything as read, without touching notifications and without recording activity. A lobby whose timer has already passed is treated as open for this answer only: it does not open the lobby and does not rename the conversation. Use the id returned in reply_to to answer and attachmentId to cite an attachment.

definitions.name: talk_reply
definitions.description: Sends a message in a conversation, optionally quoting another message of the same conversation with reply_to. To point at a Deck card or a calendar event, send reference with {type: deck_card, card_id, board_id optional} or {type: calendar_event, calendar (the path reported by calendar_list_calendars), uid}: the server checks that the user can access the item and appends the title and the link of the item to the text, and the draft already shows the final text. Anyone in the conversation who cannot access the item will see the title and the link, so only reference what the user approves showing. Preview without confirm and follow the approval method returned by the server.

definitions.name: talk_attach_file
definitions.description: Shares into the conversation a file that already exists in the user's Nextcloud; Talk itself publishes the attachment card. When message is filled in, it is sent as a second text message right after the attachment, and messageId carries the id of that message. If the file is already shared in this conversation, nothing is published. If the share is created but the caption fails, the answer is not an error: it comes with attachmentId and captionSent false plus the instruction to send the caption with talk_reply, because the attachment is already in the chat. Preview without confirm and follow the approval method returned by the server.

definitions.name: talk_quote_file
definitions.description: Publishes a message citing an attachment already present in the conversation, identified by attachment_id, with an optional caption in message. Use the attachmentId (the numeric share id) that talk_attach_file or talk_read_messages returned for that attachment, not the id of the message that carries it. Preview without confirm and follow the approval method returned by the server.

definitions.name: talk_message_user
definitions.description: Sends a direct message to a user, without needing the conversation token: send user with the account id (if you are not sure of it, call users_search first). The direct conversation is created when it does not exist yet, the way Talk does when a chat is started; the preview never creates anything. Preview without confirm and follow the approval method returned by the server.

definitions.name: talk_send_batch
definitions.description: Sends several messages at once in the same conversation, each one optionally quoting an earlier message: send messages with the list of objects {message, reply_to}. Use it when the answer is a sequence of short messages (one per item of a list, for instance), and prefer talk_reply when it is a single message. The conversation and the quotes are checked before anything is sent; sending happens item by item and each item is reported in sent or failed, without repeating what was already published. Preview without confirm and follow the approval method returned by the server. The approval covers the entire batch.

definitions.name: talk_create_group
definitions.description: Creates a group conversation in Talk, with the authenticated user as its owner: send name with the name of the group and participants with the list of accounts to invite (optional). Every guest goes through the same visibility rule as a direct message, and all of them appear in the preview before any invitation. Creating a group invites people and this tool does not undo an invitation once it has been made, so the operation requires the talk.create grant and an explicit approval. Preview without confirm and follow the approval method returned by the server. The approval covers the group name and guests together. Whoever does not approve does not get an empty group in the list: the room is only created by the approved call. The invitations are made one by one after the creation: whoever joined comes in participants and whoever Talk refused comes in invitations_failed, with the id of each one; in that case the group already exists, so do not repeat the call, tell the user who was left out.

definitions.name: talk_list_unread
definitions.description: Lists only the Talk conversations of the authenticated user that have unread messages, up to 50 per page. A conversation the lobby bars is omitted and its unread count is not returned. A lobby whose timer has already passed is treated as open for this answer only and is not written back. The list is not frozen: a conversation that receives a message between pages can change position, and nextCursor only continues after the last conversation of this page. To see everything again, call the tool once more without a cursor. It changes no state: it does not mark anything as read, does not change lastReadMessage, lastPing, the session or notifications, and it does not open a lobby or rename a conversation.

cursor.description: Continuation from the previous page of this same user. The list is not frozen: a conversation that receives a message can change position, and seeing everything again means calling without this cursor.

definitions.name: talk_read_unread
definitions.description: Reads the messages of a conversation that come after the read marker of the authenticated user, oldest first, up to 200 per page. lastReadMessage is the marker the read started from; 0 means no read is known, so the read starts at the oldest message Talk still keeps. nextCursor continues after the last message returned, so a marker moved meanwhile by another client neither skips nor repeats messages; it is null when no message remained at the time of the read. If the last message returned is removed before the next page, the cursor is refused: call again without it to start from the read marker. The pages are not a frozen mailbox: messages that arrive while paging show up in later pages, and a message deleted or expired by retention leaves no entry. A conversation hosted on another server is refused. It changes no state: it does not mark anything as read, does not change lastReadMessage, the session, the status, notifications or the lobby.

cursor.description: Continuation from the previous page of this same read: the same user and the same conversation. It continues after the last message already returned, even if the read marker moved meanwhile. Starting again from the current marker means calling without this cursor.

To point at a Deck card or a calendar event, send reference with {type: deck_card, card_id, board_id optional} or {type: calendar_event, calendar (the path reported by calendar_list_calendars), uid}: the server checks that the user can access the item and appends the title and the link of the item to the text, and the draft already shows the final text. Anyone in the conversation who cannot access the item will see the title and the link, so only reference what the user approves showing. Preview without confirm and follow the approval method returned by the server.

definitions.name: talk_attach_file
definitions.description: Shares into the conversation a file that already exists in the user's Nextcloud; Talk itself publishes the attachment card. When message is filled in, it is sent as a second text message right after the attachment, and messageId carries the id of that message. If the file is already shared in this conversation, nothing is published. If the share is created but the caption fails, the answer is not an error: it comes with attachmentId and captionSent false plus the instruction to send the caption with talk_reply, because the attachment is already in the chat. Preview without confirm and follow the approval method returned by the server.

definitions.name: talk_quote_file
definitions.description: Publishes a message citing an attachment already present in the conversation, identified by attachment_id, with an optional caption in message. Use the attachmentId (the numeric share id) that talk_attach_file or talk_read_messages returned for that attachment, not the id of the message that carries it. Preview without confirm and follow the approval method returned by the server.

definitions.name: talk_message_user
definitions.description: Sends a direct message to a user, without needing the conversation token: send user with the account id (if you are not sure of it, call users_search first). The direct conversation is created when it does not exist yet, the way Talk does when a chat is started; the preview never creates anything. Preview without confirm and follow the approval method returned by the server.

definitions.name: talk_send_batch
definitions.description: Sends several messages at once in the same conversation, each one optionally quoting an earlier message: send messages with the list of objects {message, reply_to}. Use it when the answer is a sequence of short messages (one per item of a list, for instance), and prefer talk_reply when it is a single message. The conversation and the quotes are checked before anything is sent; sending happens item by item and each item is reported in sent or failed, without repeating what was already published. Preview without confirm and follow the approval method returned by the server. The approval covers the entire batch.

definitions.name: talk_create_group
definitions.description: Creates a group conversation in Talk, with the authenticated user as its owner: send name with the name of the group and participants with the list of accounts to invite (optional). Every guest goes through the same visibility rule as a direct message, and all of them appear in the preview before any invitation. Creating a group invites people and this tool does not undo an invitation once it has been made, so the operation requires the talk.create grant and an explicit approval. Preview without confirm and follow the approval method returned by the server. The approval covers the group name and guests together. Whoever does not approve does not get an empty group in the list: the room is only created by the approved call. The invitations are made one by one after the creation: whoever joined comes in participants and whoever Talk refused comes in invitations_failed, with the id of each one; in that case the group already exists, so do not repeat the call, tell the user who was left out.

definitions.name: talk_list_unread
definitions.description: Lists only the Talk conversations of the authenticated user that have unread messages, up to 50 per page. A conversation the lobby bars is omitted and its unread count is not returned. A lobby whose timer has already passed is treated as open for this answer only and is not written back. The list is not frozen: a conversation that receives a message between pages can change position, and nextCursor only continues after the last conversation of this page. To see everything again, call the tool once more without a cursor. It changes no state: it does not mark anything as read, does not change lastReadMessage, lastPing, the session or notifications, and it does not open a lobby or rename a conversation.

cursor.description: Continuation from the previous page of this same user. The list is not frozen: a conversation that receives a message can change position, and seeing everything again means calling without this cursor.

definitions.name: talk_read_unread
definitions.description: Reads the messages of a conversation that come after the read marker of the authenticated user, oldest first, up to 200 per page. lastReadMessage is the marker the read started from; 0 means no read is known, so the read starts at the oldest message Talk still keeps. nextCursor continues after the last message returned, so a marker moved meanwhile by another client neither skips nor repeats messages; it is null when no message remained at the time of the read. If the last message returned is removed before the next page, the cursor is refused: call again without it to start from the read marker. The pages are not a frozen mailbox: messages that arrive while paging show up in later pages, and a message deleted or expired by retention leaves no entry. A conversation hosted on another server is refused. It changes no state: it does not mark anything as read, does not change lastReadMessage, the session, the status, notifications or the lobby.

cursor.description: Continuation from the previous page of this same read: the same user and the same conversation. It continues after the last message already returned, even if the read marker moved meanwhile. Starting again from the current marker means calling without this cursor.
